subject.title: [Slack] Agent lacks visibility into own channel messages from DM sessions

question: Should DM sessions receive a bounded self-authored activity query, or should operators rely on broader same-agent session visibility for cross-channel recall?
rationale: The code can support either path, but the choice determines the authorization boundary, storage owner, retention/deletion behavior, and whether shared-channel content becomes readable from DMs.

options.title: Scoped self-activity index
options.body: Add a bounded, transport-aware query over only the agent's successfully delivered outbound messages without exposing complete sibling transcripts.

options.title: Document agent visibility
options.body: Treat `tools.sessions.visibility: "agent"` plus session tools as the supported opt-in, accepting that it exposes broader same-agent transcript content.

options.title: Unify selected sessions
options.body: Pursue the broader shared-session grouping direction tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/19929, accepting larger routing and privacy changes.

recommendation.title: Scoped self-activity index
recommendation.body: Add a bounded, transport-aware query over only the agent's successfully delivered outbound messages without exposing complete sibling transcripts.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate from the current issue discussion and recent Slack transcript/session history.
